authority.note: Shot and read back in the commissioned mechanics-revision run 2026-08-08 (Gary's written brief: small orange compasses, unbranded, clay/orange family). Seed blessed in-run by the steward against the declared invariants; flag in run report for Gary's eyes. EXTENDED 2026-08-08 (portal reconstruction, Gary's direction): the compass is a SMART device the keepers parachute down in small crates; its needle always swings to the live portal. Same locked plates, same unbranded face; the extension is lore, a 'crated' render pose, and the needle's new target.

render.always: THE ORANGE COMPASS: a palm-sized round pocket compass in a burnt-clay orange enamel shell with a thin brass rim, hung on a short braided cream cord. Its face is plain warm cream with a single dark needle tipped in the same clay orange. NO letters, numbers, degree marks, logos or brand marks anywhere on it. The orange sits in this universe's own clay family, warm and matte, never neon. Warm-editorial ink-and-wash, never photoreal.

scale.size: about 45 mm across, palm-sized; hangs at the collarbone or a pack strap on its short cord, and reads as a small bright coin of clay orange at any distance

prose.lore: The keepers' answer to the smudged pages: the island's keepers want as many founders through as they can get before the portal closes, so they parachute small crates into the green, and inside each is a smart orange compass whose needle always swings toward the live portal. Rumor says the ones holding a sky-compass find the portal long before anyone else. A compass in hand plus a friend who tells you first is how a seeker makes it in time. First appears in Finders Tell Their Friends (spreads 6, 11, 15, 16). (Mechanics revised by Gary 2026-08-08: the needle's target is the portal; delivery is by parachuted crate.)
prose.rules: An unbranded object inside the fable: never a company name, never a logo, never lettering on the face, the crate or the parachute. The shell's orange is the universe's existing clay/orange family (the same family as Maya's rust scarf), matte and warm, never neon and never safety-vest orange. Small in frame almost everywhere: a palm-sized object held, hung from a pack strap, or resting on a map. 'Smart' is shown only by the needle: it always swings toward the live portal, decisively, and may glow very faintly warm in dim scenes, never like a screen. No buttons, dials, antennas or lights are ever added.
